title: pstack + Cursor Team Kit + Cursor CLI

kinds.external: Team Kit, Cursor runtime or project dependency
kinds.board: persisted state or generated local artifact

nodes.label: /setup-pstack
nodes.what: Configure the model and effort for each pstack role.
nodes.when: First install or whenever you need to change the reasoning budget or role models.
nodes.how: Detect available models, load existing choices, confirm the budget and roles, validate and write `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` with alwaysApply and defaults: 3. `auto` and `inherit-parent` omit the delegate model.

nodes.label: /poteto-mode
nodes.what: The main engineering workflow router.
nodes.when: Start any nontrivial engineering task; explicitly attach the skill or use it as a Custom Mode.
nodes.how: Restate the goal, select a matching playbook, copy its steps into the todo list and run the required skills. Apply the appropriate principle leaf files. The receiving chat owns execution; direct delegates read worker.md. Route large or unmatched work to figure-it-out.

nodes.label: /poteto-help
nodes.what: Find the right pstack workflow and a prompt to use.
nodes.when: When new to pstack or unsure which skill or playbook fits. Explicit invocation.
nodes.how: Identify the task, consult the appropriate recipe and return a usable prompt instead of executing the engineering task.

nodes.label: /in-your-own-words
nodes.what: Restate the goal before work begins.
nodes.when: When the task or intent needs a faithful playback. Explicit invocation.
nodes.how: Explain the goal and problem in the agent’s own words before starting implementation.

nodes.label: /sharpen
nodes.what: Improve the depth of a prompt before sending it.
nodes.when: When you want stronger methods, material and independent checks rather than a larger scope.
nodes.how: Return a rewritten prompt, using empirical prototypes to settle runnable questions and reserving product choices for the operator. Does not execute the task.

nodes.label: /how
nodes.what: Trace the mechanics of a subsystem.
nodes.when: When learning an unfamiliar subsystem or investigating how behavior works.
nodes.how: Read the actual implementation, follow the path and explain its moving parts and gotchas.

nodes.label: /why
nodes.what: Find historical motivation from the record.
nodes.when: When a design choice, constraint or regression needs historical explanation.
nodes.how: Trace commits and pull request discussions; attribute conclusions to the record, mark inferences and unknowns.

nodes.label: /teach
nodes.what: Combine mechanics and motivation into a coherent explanation.
nodes.when: When you want to understand a change rather than receive a summary.
nodes.how: Run how and why, then weave a plain account, using diagrams to build understanding.

nodes.label: /recall
nodes.what: Reconstruct current context from relevant chat history and shared records.
nodes.when: When starting or resuming work with previous context.
nodes.how: Recover the relevant trail and provide a concise current-state brief.

nodes.label: /ketchup
nodes.what: Explain what has changed since the previous message.
nodes.when: When returning to a long chat and needing to decide outstanding items.
nodes.how: Summarize changes, add small visuals where useful, and make each awaiting decision self-contained.

nodes.label: /ketchup-video
nodes.what: Present the ketchup recap as a short subtitled slide video.
nodes.when: When a visual catch-up is preferred.
nodes.how: Present the recap as a short video and list decisions waiting for the operator in text.

nodes.label: /architect
nodes.what: Settle a caller-facing API and module shape before implementation.
nodes.when: When a change crosses a function boundary or a one-way-door design decision needs alternatives.
nodes.how: Name types and caller usage first; use arena for competing designs, then choose the smallest coherent shape.

nodes.label: /arena
nodes.what: Run parallel competing attempts at the same artifact.
nodes.when: When one attempt at a nontrivial artifact risks locking in the wrong design.
nodes.how: Frame the same task; create isolated output locations; fan out candidates using configured runners; use a cross-vendor judge; choose a base and integrate useful parts; verify the result.

nodes.label: /swarm
nodes.what: Fan out parallel workers across slices, then aggregate.
nodes.when: When independent coverage, races, mechanical edits or a gauntlet can run concurrently.
nodes.how: Define the finish predicate and outputs; use generalPurpose workers in cloud by default, local only for local-access needs, then reconcile and verify the report.

nodes.label: /interrogate
nodes.what: Attack a diff or design with independent reviewers.
nodes.when: When an important design or change needs adversarial evidence.
nodes.how: Use arena setup and fan-out with configured reviewers; rerun each claimed failure, keep only verified findings that violate the intent; combine shared root causes.

nodes.label: /blast-radius
nodes.what: Find what a small-looking change can break.
nodes.when: Before accepting a change with uncertain downstream effects.
nodes.how: Trace affected behavior and prove the fact that makes the change safe by executing code.

nodes.label: /tdd
nodes.what: Write the failing test before the fix.
nodes.when: For bugs with an inexpensive local test path.
nodes.how: Establish a red test that reflects observable behavior, implement the fix, then demonstrate green. Skip costly or unclear repro-test paths as specified by the playbook.

nodes.label: /benchmark-checklist
nodes.what: Assess whether a measured number is trustworthy.
nodes.when: Before reporting or acting on performance measurements.
nodes.how: Check the limiting factor, workload, tuning, error modes, repeat runs and end-to-end relevance before accepting a comparison.

nodes.label: /no-comments
nodes.what: Remove unnecessary comments before review.
nodes.when: After implementation and before review.
nodes.how: Spawn Comment Sicko to examine comments, fix accepted findings and identify structural encodings for real constraints.

nodes.label: /typescript-best-practices
nodes.what: Apply type discipline in TypeScript.
nodes.when: When reading or editing TypeScript.
nodes.how: Use type-system discipline and the skill’s TypeScript patterns to keep invalid states out of the design.

nodes.label: /figure-it-out
nodes.what: Design and execute a bespoke auditable playbook.
nodes.when: For ambitious, cross-cutting, unattended or unmatched work.
nodes.how: Frame the outcome, design the workflow, use architect for consequential decisions, loop on hypotheses, log decisions via show-me-your-work and verify before handoff.

nodes.label: /show-me-your-work
nodes.what: Keep an auditable decision trail.
nodes.when: For long tasks or work that will be reviewed after stepping away.
nodes.how: Record time, phase, decision, reason, evidence and result in a TSV; commit the trail when useful to a reviewer.

nodes.label: /create-verification-skill
nodes.what: Generate a project-local skill for driving the real app.
nodes.when: When a repository lacks a scripted verification surface.
nodes.how: Inspect launch/drive/observe/isolate requirements, generate `.cursor/skills/verify-<app>/` with launch, doctor, drive, evidence and cleanup, seed a feature map, and run one feature end to end.

nodes.label: /maintain-verification-skill
nodes.what: Keep a project-local verifier and feature map current.
nodes.when: When application behavior and verification instructions have drifted.
nodes.how: Run source readers per feature, reconcile, exercise every feature in a coordinator-owned live pass, fix only verified harness or documentation drift, and ship at most one PR.

nodes.label: /create-formal-verification-skill
nodes.what: Create a project-local formal verification skill.
nodes.when: When a race, retry, protocol, parser, state machine or unsafe-code property exceeds ordinary tests.
nodes.how: Choose a suitable tool, verify a specific property and generate a repeatable project-local check.

nodes.label: /maintain-formal-verification-skill
nodes.what: Maintain a formal verification model as code changes.
nodes.when: When the implementation covered by a formal check has changed.
nodes.how: Update the model, harness or properties to correspond to the code, rerun, and distinguish verification drift from actual defects.

nodes.label: /statechart
nodes.what: Turn a checked TLA+ model into a user-facing statechart.
nodes.when: When a product or behavior owner needs to see reachable states and rule failures.
nodes.how: Check the model, draw the behavior in Mermaid, mark violating states and show a shortest path to each.

nodes.label: /reflect
nodes.what: Capture lessons from a finished task.
nodes.when: When a long task landed and its successful recipe should be reusable.
nodes.how: Review what happened and preserve the lesson as a skill edit rather than repeating the same discovery.

nodes.label: /correct
nodes.what: Eliminate recurring classes of agent mistakes.
nodes.when: When the operator keeps correcting the same kind of error.
nodes.how: Mine history, fix mistake classes at the strongest enforceable level (architecture, types, lint/CI, tests, docs) and track the rules and enforcement.

nodes.label: /automate-me
nodes.what: Draft a custom mode from observed work habits.
nodes.when: When you want a reusable -mode skill derived from actual sessions.
nodes.how: Turn recurring behavior into a mode draft. Distinct from Cursor’s /automate, which creates cloud automations.

nodes.label: /make-bot-ui
nodes.what: Create a dashboard or page that wakes a Grok Bot via webhook.
nodes.when: When you need a UI trigger for an existing Grok Bot integration.
nodes.how: Design the webhook button and sender-key handoff, including Tailscale requirements described in the skill. Optional specialized workflow, not required for pstack.

nodes.label: /unslop
nodes.what: Remove AI writing tells from prose.
nodes.when: When composing or revising replies, documentation or other prose.
nodes.how: Rewrite to remove formulaic phrasing and keep the useful facts. Distinct from Team Kit deslop, which cleans code.

nodes.label: /bro
nodes.what: Restate the previous message in ordinary language.
nodes.when: When technical jargon obstructs understanding.
nodes.how: Translate the last message into plain human language without unnecessary jargon.

nodes.label: /technical-writing
nodes.what: Apply a layered technical writing standard.
nodes.when: For docs, RFCs, READMEs, PR descriptions and commit messages.
nodes.how: Apply Diátaxis, Google developer style, Simplified Technical English and Global English as appropriate.

nodes.label: /control-ui
nodes.what: Build or adapt a browser/CDP harness for web, IDE or Electron UI.
nodes.when: When proving UI behavior or reproducing visual/performance issues.
nodes.how: Drive the real UI, use stable selection, collect screenshots, accessibility snapshots or profiles, and isolate or clean up the controlled instance.

nodes.label: /control-cli
nodes.what: Build or adapt a local interactive CLI/TUI harness.
nodes.when: When proving terminal behavior, UX, latency, memory or hangs.
nodes.how: Drive an isolated tmux or PTY session; capture transcripts, profiles and user-visible results.

nodes.label: /deslop
nodes.what: Remove generated code slop.
nodes.when: Before committing a pstack change.
nodes.how: Review the diff for redundant code, inconsistent style and unnecessary abstractions; clean the patch without expanding scope.

nodes.label: /verify-this
nodes.what: Prove or disprove a claim with fresh evidence.
nodes.when: When a claim needs baseline/treatment comparison.
nodes.how: State a falsifiable claim, capture both artifacts, compare and return VERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED or INCONCLUSIVE.

nodes.label: /loop-on-ci
nodes.what: Watch CI and iterate until checks pass.
nodes.when: When driving an active PR through failing checks.
nodes.how: Inspect runs, identify failures, make focused fixes and repeat. pstack has its own Babysit playbook.

nodes.label: /fix-ci
nodes.what: Investigate failing CI jobs.
nodes.when: When a specific CI run is red.
nodes.how: Read logs, identify the failing job and apply focused corrections.

nodes.label: /review-and-ship
nodes.what: Perform a structured review, commit and open a PR.
nodes.when: When choosing Team Kit’s independent delivery flow.
nodes.how: Review the changes, commit and create a PR; not pstack’s Shipping playbook.

nodes.label: /pr-review-canvas
nodes.what: Generate an annotated interactive PR walkthrough.
nodes.when: When a reviewer needs a categorized visual diff.
nodes.how: Render a PR walkthrough using the bundled template and renderer.

nodes.label: /make-pr-easy-to-review
nodes.what: Improve PR history, descriptions and guidance.
nodes.when: When preparing a noisy PR for a reviewer.
nodes.how: Clean noisy history and clarify the reviewer-facing explanation.

nodes.label: /run-smoke-tests
nodes.what: Run Playwright smoke tests and triage failures.
nodes.when: When the repository uses Playwright smoke coverage.
nodes.how: Execute smoke tests and diagnose failures.

nodes.label: /new-branch-and-pr
nodes.what: Create a branch, complete work and open a PR.
nodes.when: When selecting Team Kit’s independent branch-to-PR workflow.
nodes.how: Start a fresh branch and deliver the work as a PR.

nodes.label: /get-pr-comments
nodes.what: Fetch and summarize active PR comments.
nodes.when: When reviewing incoming PR feedback.
nodes.how: Retrieve review comments and summarize the findings.

nodes.label: /check-compiler-errors
nodes.what: Run compilation and type checks.
nodes.when: When compiler or typing failures need diagnosis.
nodes.how: Run the repository’s compile and type-check commands; report failures.

nodes.label: /what-did-i-get-done
nodes.what: Summarize authored commits over a time range.
nodes.when: When writing a status update.
nodes.how: Read authored commits and produce a concise summary.

nodes.label: /weekly-review
nodes.what: Summarize shipped work across the week.
nodes.when: For a weekly engineering recap.
nodes.how: Group delivered bug fixes, technical debt and new functionality.

nodes.label: /fix-merge-conflicts
nodes.what: Resolve merge conflicts and verify results.
nodes.when: When a branch has conflicts.
nodes.how: Resolve conflicts, validate the build and tests, then explain decisions.

nodes.label: /workflow-from-chats
nodes.what: Extract durable working preferences from chats.
nodes.when: When recurring work patterns merit reusable instructions.
nodes.how: Derive skills, rules or docs from chat history.

nodes.label: /thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review
nodes.what: Perform a stringent maintainability review.
nodes.when: When evaluating whether a diff is unnecessarily complicated.
nodes.how: Apply the code quality rubric to complexity, boundaries and readability.

nodes.label: ci-watcher
nodes.what: Team Kit subagent for monitoring GitHub Actions and reporting pass/fail.
nodes.when: When the corresponding Team Kit agent or rule is applicable.
nodes.how: Part of Team Kit; included as adjacent capability, not a required pstack dependency.

nodes.label: thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review
nodes.what: Team Kit subagent for maintainability review.
nodes.when: When the corresponding Team Kit agent or rule is applicable.
nodes.how: Part of Team Kit; included as adjacent capability, not a required pstack dependency.

nodes.label: typescript-exhaustive-switch
nodes.what: Team Kit rule for exhaustive union and enum switch cases.
nodes.when: When the corresponding Team Kit agent or rule is applicable.
nodes.how: Part of Team Kit; included as adjacent capability, not a required pstack dependency.

nodes.label: no-inline-imports
nodes.what: Team Kit rule requiring module-level imports.
nodes.when: When the corresponding Team Kit agent or rule is applicable.
nodes.how: Part of Team Kit; included as adjacent capability, not a required pstack dependency.

nodes.label: Cursor CLI
nodes.what: Terminal host for Cursor Agent, plugins, skills and supported execution modes.
nodes.when: When you want to run pstack in a terminal instead of the editor.
nodes.how: Install and authenticate Cursor Agent. Use `agent` interactively or `agent -p` for documented print-mode automation. Features can differ by surface.

nodes.label: Plugin management
nodes.what: Install or manage plugins and marketplaces.
nodes.when: Before relying on pstack or Team Kit skills.
nodes.how: Use Cursor plugin installation and CLI `/plugin` management. Verify both packs are available in the intended scope.

nodes.label: Custom Mode
nodes.what: Attach a skill persistently across turns.
nodes.when: When you want poteto-mode to remain active.
nodes.how: Pick poteto-mode in the slash menu; use Option+Enter or Alt+Enter to activate as a Custom Mode rather than attaching it to one message.

nodes.label: /goal
nodes.what: Persistent objective for an agent run.
nodes.when: When the agent should continue toward a checkable outcome.
nodes.how: Use `/goal <objective>`. In CLI, Ctrl+C pauses the goal. Pair with Custom Mode or /loop as appropriate. Cursor documents this feature as rolling out.

nodes.label: /loop
nodes.what: Recurring or variable-interval agent wake mechanism.
nodes.when: When waiting on events, polling CI or checking progress in autonomous-run.
nodes.how: Use a wake cadence or let the agent choose. pstack autonomous-run and visual-parity explicitly reference this built-in; /goal is a separate objective mechanism.

nodes.label: /automate
nodes.what: Cursor built-in skill to configure cloud automations.
nodes.when: When setting up a new scheduled/event-driven workflow from a local agent.
nodes.how: Describe triggers, instructions and tools. Review the draft in the editor. Benny requires explicit creation approval; no CLI availability claim is made for this skill.

nodes.label: Cloud agents
nodes.what: Isolated remote execution and asynchronous work on the Cursor platform.
nodes.when: For remote work, independent verification, or handoff from a local chat.
nodes.how: Use the cloud-agent workflow; in CLI, prepend `&` to a message to hand off to cloud. Cloud agents are not the same as local CLI print-mode processes.

nodes.label: Task / subagents
nodes.what: Cursor’s delegation mechanism.
nodes.when: When pstack delegates an implementation, panel, or parallel independent checks.
nodes.how: Delegate with the required subagent type, model, isolation and background mode. pstack direct delegates use poteto-agent; swarm and interrogate specify generalPurpose.

nodes.label: agent --worktree
nodes.what: Start a CLI run in an isolated Git worktree.
nodes.when: When running parallel changes without touching the current checkout.
nodes.how: Use `agent -w [name]` or `agent --worktree [name]`; the documented CLI worktree mechanism is distinct from pstack’s own Git worktree handling.

nodes.label: agent -p
nodes.what: Noninteractive CLI print mode for scripts and CI.
nodes.when: When running a bounded scripted agent job.
nodes.how: Use documented print mode and output formats. Set appropriate permissions and an explicit completion predicate. This is a host capability, not a pstack playbook.

nodes.label: /model
nodes.what: Select the current session’s model.
nodes.when: When setting the parent model or checking available choices.
nodes.how: Use the CLI model selector; pstack setup writes a separate role configuration for delegates.

nodes.label: MCP
nodes.what: Configured external tools and integrations.
nodes.when: When workflows need additional services or tools.
nodes.how: CLI respects MCP configuration; use `/mcp` to inspect server/tool availability. Integration and permissions must be configured.

nodes.label: /resume
nodes.what: Resume a prior CLI chat.
nodes.when: When continuing a prior session.
nodes.how: Select a recent conversation using /resume. This is a host command; pstack session-pickup reconstructs work state and routes unfinished work.

nodes.label: /summarize
nodes.what: Compress conversation context.
nodes.when: When a long chat needs context relief.
nodes.how: Use /summarize (alias /compress). The pstack pause-safely playbook can preserve a separate off-context resume note.

nodes.label: Cursor rules & skills
nodes.what: Persistent rules and agent skill discovery.
nodes.when: When sharing role choices, project constraints and plugin skills.
nodes.how: Cursor loads configured rules and skills; CLI also reads `.cursor/rules`, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md where supported.

nodes.label: create-skill
nodes.what: Cursor built-in skill authoring helper.
nodes.when: When pstack’s authoring-a-skill playbook is selected.
nodes.how: Use the built-in authoring skill, validate frontmatter, file references and cross-skill links, and test structural cases.

nodes.label: Bugbot
nodes.what: Cursor’s PR review service.
nodes.when: When bot feedback appears on a PR.
nodes.how: Treat findings as claims to verify, fix real problems and dismiss unsupported ones with evidence; availability depends on configuration.

nodes.label: Cloud Automations
nodes.what: Scheduled or event-triggered cloud agent execution.
nodes.when: When work should start from a timer or service event, not a live chat.
nodes.how: Configure triggers, instructions and tools, then enable a reviewed automation. Benny is one dormant automation pack built on this service.

nodes.label: poteto-agent
nodes.what: pstack’s wrapper for direct Task delegates.
nodes.when: When poteto-mode directly spawns a worker.
nodes.how: Read the poteto-mode instructions in full. The receiving chat remains the playbook owner, and special routed skills may set a different subagent type.

nodes.label: Comment Sicko
nodes.what: Read-only specialist for comment review.
nodes.when: When no-comments calls its comment reviewer.
nodes.how: Review the diff for unnecessary comments and report findings to the caller.

nodes.label: worker.md
nodes.what: Shared instructions for every pstack delegate.
nodes.when: At the start of a Task or Project worker.
nodes.how: The kickoff’s first line points to the absolute worker.md path. Preserve the operator’s gates, avoid unnecessary blocking, use ready PRs and follow the PR writing format.

nodes.label: pstack-models.mdc
nodes.what: User-scoped always-applied model selection rule.
nodes.when: After setup-pstack writes configuration.
nodes.how: The rule contains a defaults marker, budget and per-role model selections; roles not present retain defaults.

nodes.label: Decision log
nodes.what: TSV recording evidence and decisions.
nodes.when: During long or unattended work.
nodes.how: Record outcome, change, rationale, evidence and result. The specific playbook determines whether the trail is local or committed.

nodes.label: verify-<app>
nodes.what: Generated project-local verification skill and feature map.
nodes.when: When real app verification must be repeatable.
nodes.how: Launch, doctor, drive, capture evidence, clean up; maintain coverage as the app evolves.

nodes.label: Formal verifier
nodes.what: Generated project-local property checks.
nodes.when: When repeatable formal verification is needed.
nodes.how: Run the chosen proof tool and maintain correspondence with actual source.

nodes.label: watch-pr
nodes.what: Bundled GitHub PR watcher.
nodes.when: Babysit and Shipping need current checks or queued-stack status.
nodes.how: Use the script under the poteto-mode scripts directory for GitHub; Origin follows its own command path.

nodes.label: worktree-audit.sh
nodes.what: Audit candidate worktrees before removal.
nodes.when: During worktree-cleanup.
nodes.how: Read Git worktree paths and classify candidates; active and pinned chats and uncommitted work override automated advice.

nodes.label: GitHub / Origin PRs
nodes.what: Source-control delivery state.
nodes.when: When opening, babysitting or shipping PRs.
nodes.how: Use gh by default; use origin pr when Origin can resolve the repository. No Graphite requirement. pstack shipping validates the contiguous verified run and honors operator permission.

nodes.label: Read-only investigation
nodes.what: Playbook: investigation. Read-only investigation.
nodes.when: Question about mechanics, motivation or a recommendation.
nodes.how: Trace code, use why for motivation, report in a clear structure and apply unslop.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Reproduce and fix
nodes.what: Playbook: bug-fix. Reproduce and fix.
nodes.when: A real defect or regression.
nodes.how: Reproduce on the matching surface; narrow causes with evidence; consult why; architect if the boundary changes; delegate; prove the original repro passes; use tdd when cheap; open a PR.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Measured performance issue
nodes.what: Playbook: perf-issue. Measured performance issue.
nodes.when: Latency, throughput or another measured slowdown.
nodes.how: Capture baseline trace with the matching control surface; vet it with benchmark-checklist; trace and delegate the fix; capture post-fix trace, compare and open a PR.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Metric optimization loop
nodes.what: Playbook: hillclimb. Metric optimization loop.
nodes.when: Sustained scientific improvement toward a fixed metric target.
nodes.how: Ground workload and architecture, freeze a sensitive harness, keep decision log, run one hypothesis at a time, keep only measured behavior-preserving wins, open a PR.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Live runtime diagnosis
nodes.what: Playbook: runtime-forensics. Live runtime diagnosis.
nodes.when: Leak, idle CPU spin or visual glitch.
nodes.how: Capture profile, snapshot or trace on matching surface; reduce it to a cause, prove the mechanism, link it to source. Read-only.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Captured artifact diagnosis
nodes.what: Playbook: trace-forensics. Captured artifact diagnosis.
nodes.when: A trace, heap snapshot or profiling artifact.
nodes.how: Parse into a queryable shape, narrow and attribute to source, compare paired captures if available; report without fixing unless requested.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: New behavior
nodes.what: Playbook: feature. New behavior.
nodes.when: A new feature or changed behavior.
nodes.how: Trace the subsystem, use architect for the shape, record throughput checkpoints, delegate a scoped change, verify the real surface, order commits, interrogate contested design, open a PR.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Behavior-preserving change
nodes.what: Playbook: refactoring. Behavior-preserving change.
nodes.when: A structural change without behavior change.
nodes.how: Pin behavior, name the target structure, subtract before adding, move in checked slices, prove equivalence and lower reader load, open a PR.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Throwaway decision artifact
nodes.what: Playbook: prototype. Throwaway decision artifact.
nodes.when: A design or empirical fork that can be settled by running something.
nodes.how: Name the decision, create isolated lightweight alternatives, observe them on the correct surface, report tradeoffs and hand chosen direction to Feature.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Pixel-exact parity
nodes.what: Playbook: visual-parity. Pixel-exact parity.
nodes.when: Matching two visual implementations or a migration baseline.
nodes.how: Capture baseline, preserve harness and baseline, parallelize isolated components, compare image diffs on real surface and loop until zero, open a PR.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Write or edit a skill
nodes.what: Playbook: authoring-a-skill. Write or edit a skill.
nodes.when: A new or modified SKILL.md.
nodes.how: Use built-in create-skill; validate frontmatter, paths and cross-links; run structural cases; open a PR.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Blinded skill / prompt evaluation
nodes.what: Playbook: eval. Blinded skill / prompt evaluation.
nodes.when: Comparing variants of a skill or prompt.
nodes.how: Frame judge-only rubric, sanitize candidate environments, give the same organic prompt, use arena fan-out and blinded judge, verify actual transcript reads, inspect every output.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Drive PR to merge-ready
nodes.what: Playbook: babysit. Drive PR to merge-ready.
nodes.when: PR conflicts, comments or red CI.
nodes.how: Resolve forge, watch current PR state, investigate and fix failures, triage Bugbot findings skeptically and report merge readiness.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Land verified run bottom-up
nodes.what: Playbook: shipping. Land verified run bottom-up.
nodes.when: Explicit authorization to land a stack.
nodes.how: Verify each PR independently with cloud agent on matching surface, determine contiguous verified ceiling, check patch identity and current checks, land bottom-up and stop at the ceiling.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Run to a predicate
nodes.what: Playbook: autonomous-run. Run to a predicate.
nodes.when: A long task with a checkable exit condition.
nodes.how: State predicate, choose /loop wake policy, make small evidence-driven changes, verify each iteration and log decisions, stop on actual completion or real dead end.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Independent PR program
nodes.what: Playbook: autopilot-full. Independent PR program.
nodes.when: Authorized queue of independently landable PRs.
nodes.how: One cloud owner per PR off trunk; code-ready after deslop/no-comments; independent swarm verifies patches; current head CI stays green; only authorized, verified patches merge. Coordinator audits with /loop.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Verified handoff, no merge
nodes.what: Playbook: autopilot-stack. Verified handoff, no merge.
nodes.when: Work queue where the operator owns landing.
nodes.how: Follow autopilot-full with no merges; stack only actual dependencies, rebase and recheck affected patches, stop verified and green and hand back to operator.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Recover prior work
nodes.what: Playbook: session-pickup. Recover prior work.
nodes.when: Taking over or resuming an interrupted run.
nodes.how: Locate prior trail, reconstruct branch and todos, determine done versus pending, route remaining task and verify inherited claims on real artifact.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Suspend without loss
nodes.what: Playbook: pause-safely. Suspend without loss.
nodes.when: Pausing or handling impending context compaction.
nodes.how: Stop at safe boundary, cancel nested work, avoid irreversible action, commit WIP locally, write resume note or point at decision log.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Plan dependent PR slices
nodes.what: Playbook: multi-phase-plan. Plan dependent PR slices.
nodes.when: Large change spanning phases or stacked PRs.
nodes.how: Prototype unsettled choices; write a dependency graph and per-PR scope, tests and live/perf predicates; stop for explicit go before execution.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Reclaim disk safely
nodes.what: Playbook: worktree-cleanup. Reclaim disk safely.
nodes.when: Merged or abandoned worktrees and simulator clutter.
nodes.how: Audit candidates, cross-check pinned and active chat state, stop on uncommitted work or uncertain ownership, remove confirmed safe candidates and verify disk usage.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Prepare a ready PR
nodes.what: Playbook: opening-a-pr. Prepare a ready PR.
nodes.when: At the end of an applicable delivery playbook.
nodes.how: Use a worktree off trunk and ordered commits, run Team Kit deslop before commit and follow the pstack PR writing and verification contract.
nodes.origin: pstack playbook · not a slash skill

nodes.label: Setup Benny
nodes.what: Install dormant Benny automation sources into the target repository.
nodes.when: Operator points Cursor at FOR_AGENTS.md and names a target repository.
nodes.how: Merge pack into `.cursor/automations/benny/`, preserve local configuration, enable project-scoped pstack and verify dependencies in a fresh agent. Commit prerequisites; create drafts only when explicitly authorized.

nodes.label: Triage issue reports
nodes.what: Classify a top-level Slack report and route it.
nodes.when: A configured top-level issue-channel report arrives.
nodes.how: Read thread and attachments, locate likely owning layer, search tracker for duplicates, create only clear net-new bugs, reply once in the original thread with a trusted marker.

nodes.label: Reproduce & fix
nodes.what: Prove confirmed bugs and optionally prepare a draft fix.
nodes.when: When the trusted triage marker identifies a bug or performance issue.
nodes.how: Respect existing ownership or PRs, reproduce on real UI twice, capture evidence and state cross-check, make one bounded root-cause fix when justified, open only a draft PR with passing before/after proof. Never merge or deploy.

nodes.label: Benny config & feature map
nodes.what: User-owned secret-free configuration outside copied pack.
nodes.when: Before enabling either automation.
nodes.how: Set Slack source and optional operations channel, tracker, repo, feature map, adapter, models and budgets; retain secrets separately. Fail closed when a required input is missing.

nodes.label: Control adapter
nodes.what: Configured app-specific harness for Benny verification.
nodes.when: For live reproducibility and before/after proof.
nodes.how: Benny requires a configured control skill or adapter and feature map; Team Kit control skills are examples of compatible surfaces, not mandatory Benny install dependencies.

nodes.label: Slack + tracker
nodes.what: Configured issue report, thread coordinates, marker and tracker state.
nodes.when: At event intake and follow-up.
nodes.how: Keep channel and root thread immutable; post only in the original thread, not a root message. Subagents do not receive Slack credentials or post.
